records.title: Dr. Lesleigh Owen and Oliver Johnson Some Politics of Period Poverty
records.description: Geek Speak is back for fall. Please join us on Mondays at 4:00 p.m. in Jonas 110 for a new topic each week: November 2: Dr. Denice Turner A Field Guide to Faults A Field Guide to Faults invites readers into the changing landscape of love after upheaval. Through stories from A Beginner's Guide to Faults, this presentation explores the emotional terrain revealed by betrayal, fidelity, grace, and forgiveness. Rather than offering prescriptions, it offers a way of noticing—of recognizing the fault lines that run through every life and discovering how they can become places of deeper understanding, compassion, and hope. November 9: Dr. Lesleigh Owen and Oliver Johnson Some Politics of Period Poverty Why does discussing menstruation make us uncomfortable? Why are toilet paper, water, and soap provided free in public bathrooms while menstrual products are often unavailable or require purchase? Surely everyone can afford menstrual products every month... right? How does period poverty affect college students' education, health, and well-being? What would change if menstrual products were treated as necessities rather than optional consumer goods? Join Oliver Johnson and Dr. Lesleigh Owen as they explore the social, economic, and cultural dimensions of period poverty. Learn how stigma, inequality, and access shape the experiences of menstruating individuals, examine research on the impact of period poverty among college students, and discover what we are doing on campus to address this often-overlooked issue. Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of the problem and practical ideas for creating change in their own communities. November 16: Dr. Breon Derby Knotty Habit: A Stress-Relief Workshop for Happy Hookers It is time to unplug from the endless notifications, step away from the screen, and pick up a new kind of coping mechanism: a Knotty Habit Knotty Habit is a chill, zero-pressure workshop designed to help you de-stress through fiber arts--crochet, cross-stitch, and embroidery. Learn how hands-on crafting helps with anxiety, slashes cortisol, and lets you make cool stuff. Nerd out on the science behind crafting and practice the basics at your own pace. Zero experience needed and all supplies provided. Let’s get knotty! To ensure we have enough supplies, an RSVP would be appreciated; please text 605-641-0668 Questions? Contact Dr. Courtney Huse Wika at Courtney.HuseWika@BHSU.edu

records.title: Workshop: Make Your Slideshow Accessible
records.description: Do you use PowerPoint, Google Slides, or other slideshow tools to teach? Have you been told to “check reading order” or fix “slide titles” in your Panorama reports? Are you unsure how to handle complex graphics like charts or detailed images? Join this workshop to learn the basics of accessible slides. Bring a slide-deck you know you will use in a future class; leave with a fixed file and a new toolset for avoiding accessibility challenges when drafting or editing slides in the future. When: Thursday, Nov 12th, 3:00pm-4:15pm Where: JA 103A (online option available when you RSVP)

records.title: Join Henry's Books for "He Sapa: Poetry, History, & Storytelling"
records.description: Join Henry's Books at the High Plains Western Heritage Center on Thursday, November 19 from 6 pm to 8 pm for our final event in our Community History Series, “He Sapa: Poetry, History, and Storytelling”. We have some great expert panelists who will be sure to inspire & remind you of the beautiful sacredness of The Hills, including local Indigenous poets & activists, long-time forest service employee, scholars of Native American literature & BHSU's own Dr. Rosie Sprague! This event is free to the public, + The Henry’s Books Foundation will be sponsoring books for all who attend!

records.title: Madrigal Dinner
records.description: Date: December 3-5, 2026 Time: Social hour at 5:30PM and dinner at 6:30PM Where: Meier Hall The event features a 20-member vocal ensemble performing early Renaissance music in costume as a sixteenth-century royal court. Guests will enjoy a holiday meal and entertainment that includes a recorder ensemble, herald trumpets, silly humor, and a short post-dinner concert. The concert will include music by Johann Hermann Schein, Ralph Vaughan Williams, Cristóbal de Morales, John Dowland, and others. During dinner, the ensemble and court jester will perform traditional carols such as Deck the Halls, A Wassail Song, and Silent Night. Dinner is $65 per person and includes: Starter: Roasted pumpkin soup with maple-glazed pecans and toasted coconut Entrée: Pork chop stuffed with bacon, smoked Gouda, and apple, served with cranberry wild rice stuffing and roasted tri-colored baby carrots Dessert: Red wine-poached pear with Amaretto crème anglaise and candied pecans Please mention any dietary needs, such as vegetarian meals or nut allergies, when making your reservation. For questions, contact Katherine Kemp at 605.642.6420 (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.)
